name: Kidgrie, or Dry Curry
description: Historical recipe from The Canadian Family Cook Book (1914). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

instructions.text: Cut a fowl into pieces the size of a walnut, put into a stewpan with a little lard and stir until nearly cooked
Cut onions into thin slices, place them in another stewpan with a little lard or butter, grill until nicely browned
When browned, add a little more butter or lard, with curry; stir a few minutes
Add the contents of the two saucepans together and stir until the meat is sufficiently cooked
After adding a teacup of water, allow to stand a short time before serving

source.author: Grace E. Denison
source.originalInstructions:
1. Cut a fowl into pieces the size of a walnut, put into a stewpan with a little lard and stir until nearly cooked
2. Cut onions into thin slices, place them in another stewpan with a little lard or butter, grill until nicely browned
3. When browned, add a little more butter or lard, with curry; stir a few minutes
4. Add the contents of the two saucepans together and stir until the meat is sufficiently cooked
5. After adding a teacup of water, allow to stand a short time before serving
